institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The geographical location, the cultural environment, the academic environment of the receiving institution, the courses offered at the institution, the academic reputation of the institution.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find the required information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received little assistance, except for when i reached out to the administration at Sciences Po regarding switching courses.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied for housing through Cité Universitaire (CIUP). This process was relatively easy and I definitely recommend anyone coming to Paris for their exchange to apply for housing through the Danish house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: At Sciences Po there are no options to live off campus. However, the community offered by the Cité has some of the same advantages as campus life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration process at Sciences Po is relatively chaotic. The exchange students are only allowed to sign up for classes where there are free spaces after the local students have signed up. 

However, the process is relatively fine if you prepare lists of potential courses before the registration process begins. 

There are, though, very little guarantee that you will get the courses that you initially want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange students were connected to two academic advisors that they could reach over email for assistance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in registering for 2/5 of the classes that I had initially wanted. However, the classes I ended up with were also fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise furture students to prepare a list of courses of interest, so they are able to search for specific courses in the registration process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: At Paris School of Internation Affairs the academic level of the courses varied greatly from lecturer to lecturer. Some lectureres were practitioners and offered a much lover level of academic content within the courses, whereas other lectureres offered courses with similar levels to those provided at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching also varied greatly from lecturer to lecturer. Some had a more interactive style of teaching, expecting the students to engage actively in all classes, whereas others had a more stringent style of teaching, where they lectured for the full 2 hour sessions without much interaction from the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Experimentation in the Social Sciences
Democracy, parties and elections in Europe
Political Economy of the Middle East: Financial Pressures, Economic Transitions and Reforms
China's Economic Transformations since 1978 in Historical and Regional perspectives
EU Trade Policy: Navigating Uncertainty

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the courses Experimentation in the Social Sciences and Democracy, parties and elections in Europe as I found that these had the highest level of academic content and I felt my learning outcome was largest. 

Political Economy of the Middle East: Financial Pressures, Economic Transitions and Reforms was also an interesting course; however, it does require a high degree of prior knowledge of the Middle East.

questions.answer: I ended up spending much more than expected on eating out as my accomodation did not have a good kitchen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was less expensive than expected as I got accommodation through the Cité in a reasonably priced house.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sciences Po has plenty of clubs and non-academic activities - often multiple times a week that one can attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend attending the after works organised by the clubs at Sciences Po.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend that they visit the many parks and museeums Paris has to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. The higher degree of bureaucracy and lower degree of structure to their courses and assignment descriptions did cause some friction during the stay.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak to your course mates both and attend club/non-academic activities organised by Sciences Po.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lower level of structure to the academic environment.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The encouragement to engage more actively in some of the courses.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be well prepared for the course registration process (prepare a list of courses of interest, consider what is important for you about the courses, e.g. content, exam format, time of the courses etc.). 

Be prapared that the exams are to a much higher degree structured by the individual lecturer resulting in little streamlining between different assignments and courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The insight into how another academic institution functions and what characterises and defines academic education outside of Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Course registration - however, it is not as challenging as it might seem when you are first introduced to the process by your academic advisors.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
